widget.successFeedback: 56 markers — the hidden total, ready for the 12 lost ones to come off it once.
widget.partialFeedback: Every pack holds the same 8 markers; build each bar to 8.

predict.prompt: 7 packs of 8, then 12 lost. Is it 7 × (8 − 12)?
predict.reveal: Removing 12 from every pack would empty them; the twelve come off the whole collection once.

cml.actionGoal: Name the quantity each step produces, then carry it into the next for g4ms two ops.
invariants: Each step of a multi-step problem produces a quantity the story never states, and the next step consumes it, which is why naming the intermediate value is what makes g4ms two ops checkable at all.
misconceptions: Applying the second step to every group instead of the whole, reading "times as many" as "more than", or reporting a quotient when the story needs the partial group rounded up.
cml.counterfactualPrompt: If the second step were applied to each group instead of the total, how far off would the answer be?

widget.prompt: A class buys 7 boxes of 7 pencils and uses 5. How many pencils remain?

commonErrors.feedback: That reported the total bought; the 5 used never came out of it.
Using pencils removes them, so the second step subtracts rather than adds.

widget.prompt: "7 packs of 8 markers, then 12 markers are lost." Which equation records it?

options.feedback: Correct — build the total first, then remove the 12 once from the whole collection.
That removes 12 from EVERY pack, which would leave a negative count in each one.
Adding a pack count to a pack size mixes two different quantities; 7 packs OF 8 multiply.
Losing markers reduces the total, so the second step subtracts.
